reason: The text explicitly describes the systematic oppression and persecution of the Hebrew people (Israelites) in Egypt. Key passages include: the Egyptians enslaving the Israelites with harshness ('וַיַּעֲבִדוּ מִצְרַיִם אֶת־ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּפָרֶךְ'), making their lives bitter with hard labor ('וַיְמָרְרוּ אֶת־ חַיֵּיהֶם בַּעֲבֹדָה קָשָׁה'), the Pharaoh's command to kill all Hebrew male infants, and the groaning and cries of the oppressed people ('וַיִּשְׁמַע אֱלֹהִים אֶת־ נַאֲקָתָם'). The entire passage documents their enslavement, persecution, and the divine response to their suffering.
